grammar: n. 好读物；引人入胜的书或文章。
collocations: a good read; a funny read; a quick read
commonMistake: read 作名词表示读物时可数；a good read 不能写成 a reading good。

example.english: This adventure story is a good read for young readers.
example.chinese: 这部冒险故事很适合年轻读者阅读。

application.prompt: This adventure story is ___; I finished it in one day. A. a good read B. a reading good
application.solution: A。解析：读起来有趣、让人很快读完的书可称为 a good read。

grammar: n. 冒险；冒险经历。常作可数名词。
collocations: an adventure; go on an adventure; an adventure story
commonMistake: 表示一次冒险通常用 an adventure；不要漏掉元音音素前的 an。

example.english: The children went on an adventure in the forest.
example.chinese: 孩子们在森林里经历了一次冒险。

application.prompt: The story is full of danger and excitement. What an ___! A. advertisement B. adventure
application.solution: B。解析：充满危险与刺激的经历是 adventure（冒险）。

grammar: n. 幻想；奇幻作品。表示一种作品时可数。
collocations: a fantasy novel; fantasy films; a world of fantasy
commonMistake: fantasy 指想象出来的世界或作品；不要与事实类的 history 混淆。

example.english: My sister enjoys reading fantasy novels about magic.
example.chinese: 我姐姐喜欢读关于魔法的奇幻小说。

application.prompt: A story about dragons and magic is a kind of ___. A. history B. fantasy
application.solution: B。解析：龙和魔法属于想象内容，因此是 fantasy（奇幻作品）。

grammar: n. 悬疑故事；神秘的事物；奥秘。
collocations: a mystery story; solve a mystery; remain a mystery
commonMistake: 表示“解开谜团”用 solve a mystery；不说 answer a mystery。

example.english: The twins tried to solve the mystery of the missing key.
example.chinese: 这对双胞胎试图解开钥匙失踪之谜。

application.prompt: No one knows who took the painting. It is still a ___. A. schedule B. mystery
application.solution: B。解析：原因尚不清楚的事情是 mystery（谜团）。

grammar: n. 小说；虚构作品。通常作不可数名词。
collocations: science fiction; a work of fiction; fiction and non-fiction
commonMistake: fiction 通常不加复数 -s；具体一部作品可说 a work/story of fiction。

example.english: The library has a large collection of science fiction.
example.chinese: 这家图书馆收藏了大量科幻小说。

application.prompt: A story invented by an author is a work of ___. A. fiction B. furniture
application.solution: A。解析：作者虚构的故事属于 fiction（小说、虚构作品）。

grammar: n. 侦探；警探。作定语时可修饰 story/novel。
collocations: a detective story; a police detective; detective fiction
commonMistake: detective 可指侦探，也可作定语；detective story 是“侦探故事”。

example.english: The detective found a clue beside the window.
example.chinese: 侦探在窗边找到了一条线索。

application.prompt: The police officer searched for clues to solve the crime. He was a ___. A. novelist B. detective
application.solution: B。解析：调查案件并寻找线索的人是 detective（侦探）。

grammar: n. 外星人；外国人。常见中考用法为“外星人”。
collocations: an alien; alien life; an alien visitor
commonMistake: alien 作“外星人”时是名词；不要因词尾 -n 把它误作形容词。

example.english: The film tells the story of an alien who visits Earth.
example.chinese: 这部电影讲述了一位外星人造访地球的故事。

application.prompt: In the film, a creature from another planet visits Earth. It is an ___. A. alien B. engine
application.solution: A。解析：来自其他星球的生物是 alien（外星人）。

grammar: n. 攻击；v. 攻击。作动词时可直接接宾语。
collocations: attack a person; launch an attack; an attack on the town
commonMistake: attack 作动词是及物动词，后面直接接对象；不说 attack to sb。

example.english: The dog barked but did not attack the visitors.
example.chinese: 那只狗吠叫了，但没有攻击来访者。

application.prompt: The soldiers began to ___ the empty fort at dawn. A. arrive B. attack
application.solution: B。解析：士兵对堡垒发起进攻，用 attack。

grammar: phr. 听说；得知。常用于询问是否知道某人或某事。
collocations: hear of a writer; have you ever heard of...?; never hear of
commonMistake: hear of 表示“听说过、知道”；hear from 表示“收到某人的来信或消息”。

example.english: Have you ever heard of the writer Mark Twain?
example.chinese: 你听说过作家马克·吐温吗？

application.prompt: I know the name, but I have never ___ that book. A. heard of B. heard from
application.solution: A。解析：询问是否听说过某本书，用 hear of；hear from 后通常接人。

grammar: n. 王国；领域。复数为 kingdoms。
collocations: a kingdom; the animal kingdom; rule a kingdom
commonMistake: 表示“王国”时是可数名词；谈一个王国要用 a/the kingdom。

example.english: The young queen ruled the kingdom for many years.
example.chinese: 年轻的女王统治这个王国多年。

application.prompt: The king ruled a large ___. A. kitchen B. kingdom
application.solution: B。解析：国王统治的地方是 kingdom（王国）。

grammar: adj. 历史的；与历史有关的。
collocations: historical facts; a historical novel; a historical building
commonMistake: historical 修饰名词；history 是名词，historically 是副词。

example.english: We visited several historical buildings in the old town.
example.chinese: 我们参观了老城区的几座历史建筑。

application.prompt: The museum displays objects from the past in a __ exhibition. A. history B. historical
application.solution: B。解析：名词 exhibition 前需用形容词 historical（历史的）。

grammar: n. 力；武力；v. 强迫；迫使。
collocations: physical force; force sb to do sth; force open a door
commonMistake: force sb to do sth 中不定式带 to；不要写 force sb do sth。

example.english: The heavy wind forced us to stay indoors.
example.chinese: 大风迫使我们待在室内。

application.prompt: The strong storm ___ us to stay indoors yesterday. A. force B. forced
application.solution: B。解析：yesterday 表示过去时间，force 的过去式是 forced；force sb to do sth 表示迫使某人做某事。

grammar: v. 偷；窃取。steal—stole—stolen。
collocations: steal a bike; steal sth from sb; have sth stolen
commonMistake: steal 表示“偷走某物”，句型为 steal sth from sb/place；过去分词是 stolen。

example.english: Someone stole my phone from the desk yesterday.
example.chinese: 昨天有人从桌上偷走了我的手机。

application.prompt: A stranger took my phone without asking while I was asleep. Someone ___ it from my bag. A. borrowed B. stole
application.solution: B。解析：未经允许拿走手机是偷窃，steal 的过去式是 stole。

grammar: v. 惩罚；处罚。
collocations: punish sb for sth; punish a student; be punished
commonMistake: 表示因某事惩罚某人用 punish sb for sth；不要误用介词 of。

example.english: The coach punished the player for arriving late.
example.chinese: 教练因那名队员迟到而惩罚了他。

application.prompt: The boy was ___ for breaking the classroom window. A. punished B. praised
application.solution: A。解析：打破窗户后受到惩罚，应用 punish 的过去分词 punished。

grammar: n. 习语；成语。复数 idioms。
collocations: a common idiom; an English idiom; use an idiom
commonMistake: idiom 是可数名词；谈一个习语时用 an idiom。

example.english: “A piece of cake” is an English idiom meaning something easy.
example.chinese: “小菜一碟”是一个表示事情容易的英语习语。

application.prompt: “Break the ice” is an English ___. A. idiom B. insect
application.solution: A。解析：固定的习惯表达叫 idiom（习语）。

examTags: 语法·现在完成时提示词
grammar: adv. 最近；不久前。常与现在完成时或一般过去时连用。
collocations: recently published; have recently moved; until recently
commonMistake: recently 可与现在完成时连用；不要把它当形容词修饰名词，形容词是 recent。

example.english: I have recently joined the school reading club.
example.chinese: 我最近加入了学校读书俱乐部。

application.prompt: They have ___ moved to a new house. A. recent B. recently
application.solution: B。解析：修饰 moved 的副词应为 recently。

examTags: 词汇·形容词与过去分词
grammar: adj. 迷路的；丢失的；失去的；也是 lose 的过去式和过去分词。
collocations: get lost; feel lost; a lost key
commonMistake: lost 可表示“迷路的”或“丢失的”；lose 是动词原形，不能放在 be 后作表语。

example.english: We got lost in the old streets but found the station later.
example.chinese: 我们在老街里迷了路，但后来找到了车站。

application.prompt: Without a map, the tourists soon got ___. A. losing B. lost
application.solution: B。解析：get lost 表示“迷路”。

grammar: phr. 迷路；走失。常用 get lost 表示进入迷路状态。
collocations: get lost in the city; get lost on the way; help sb who is lost
commonMistake: get lost 中 lost 是形容词；描述迷路状态用 get/be lost，不说 get lose。

example.english: We got lost because we took the wrong road.
example.chinese: 我们因为走错路而迷路了。

application.prompt: They took the wrong turn and ___ in the forest. A. got lost B. got losing
application.solution: A。解析：表示“迷路了”用 get lost。

grammar: v. 推荐；建议。可接名词，也可接 doing。
collocations: recommend a book; recommend sth to sb; recommend doing sth
commonMistake: recommend 后接动名词作宾语，如 recommend reading；不说 recommend to do。

example.english: My teacher recommended this novel to me.
example.chinese: 老师向我推荐了这本小说。

application.prompt: Our teacher ___ visiting the science museum. A. recommended B. refused
application.solution: A。解析：recommend doing sth 表示“建议做某事”。

grammar: n. 社会；社团。通常 society 表示“社会”时不可数。
collocations: modern society; a reading society; society as a whole
commonMistake: 表示“现代社会”时 society 前一般不加冠词；形容词形式是 social。

example.english: Reading can help us understand society better.
example.chinese: 阅读能帮助我们更好地了解社会。

application.prompt: Schools play an important role in modern ___. A. social B. society
application.solution: B。解析：介词 in 后需要名词 society（社会）。

grammar: adj. 文学的；文学上的。
collocations: literary works; a literary magazine; literary history
commonMistake: literary 是形容词，literature 是名词；不要把 literary 与 literal（字面的）混淆。

example.english: The magazine publishes literary works by young writers.
example.chinese: 这本杂志刊登年轻作家的文学作品。

application.prompt: The library holds a ___ event for local writers. A. literary B. literature
application.solution: A。解析：修饰 event 要用形容词 literary。

grammar: n. 基础；基地；v. 以……为基础；设立总部。
collocations: the base of a tower; a military base; be based in London
commonMistake: base sth on sth 表示“以……为依据”；be based in 表示“以……为基地”。

example.english: The company is based in Shanghai.
example.chinese: 这家公司总部设在上海。

application.prompt: The story is ___ a real event. A. basing on B. based on
application.solution: B。解析：be based on 表示“以……为基础”。

examTags: 语法·被动结构 be based on
grammar: phr. 以某事为根据；把某事建立在……基础上。
collocations: base an opinion on facts; base a story on real life; be based on
commonMistake: 主动句用 base A on B；被动句用 A be based on B，介词 on 不可省略。

example.english: The film is based on a story from a local newspaper.
example.chinese: 这部电影改编自当地报纸上的一个故事。

application.prompt: The writer ___ the character on her childhood friend. A. based B. depended
application.solution: A。解析：base sth on sth 表示“以某事为基础”；base 后的宾语是 character。

sources.label: Cambridge Dictionary: base sth on sth

grammar: n. 总结；概要。复数 summaries。
collocations: write a summary; a short summary; in summary
commonMistake: summary 的复数是 summaries（y 变 i 加 -es）；动词是 summarize。

example.english: Please write a short summary of the chapter.
example.chinese: 请写一段本章的简短概要。

application.prompt: At the end of the report, she added a brief ___. A. summary B. summarize
application.solution: A。解析：形容词 brief 后需名词 summary。

examTags: 词汇·形容词与过去分词
grammar: adj. 被宠坏的；娇惯坏的。也可作 spoil 的过去式或过去分词。
collocations: a spoiled child; spoiled food; be spoiled by sb
commonMistake: spoiled 可作形容词；spoil 的过去式和过去分词也可写作 spoilt，注意 spoiled food 意为变质的食物。

example.english: The spoiled child expected everyone to do what he wanted.
example.chinese: 这个被宠坏的孩子希望每个人都照他的意思做。

application.prompt: The child is rude because he has been too ___. A. spoil B. spoiled
application.solution: B。解析：完成时被动结构 has been 后接过去分词 spoiled。

grammar: adj. 自私的。名词形式 selfishness。
collocations: a selfish act; selfish behaviour; be selfish
commonMistake: selfish 描述人或行为；不要与 selfless（无私的）混淆。

example.english: It was selfish of him to keep all the food for himself.
example.chinese: 他把所有食物都留给自己，真自私。

application.prompt: Sharing the prize with nobody was a ___ choice. A. selfish B. helpful
application.solution: A。解析：只顾自己、不与人分享是 selfish（自私的）。

grammar: adj. 令人痛苦的；（身体部位）疼痛的。
collocations: a painful injury; a painful memory; feel painful
commonMistake: painful 是形容词，pain 是名词；描述某人感到疼通常说 be in pain 或 have a painful arm。

example.english: The fall left him with a painful knee.
example.chinese: 那次摔倒让他的膝盖很疼。

application.prompt: The cut was so ___ that he went to see a doctor. A. pain B. painful
application.solution: B。解析：be 动词后作表语要用形容词 painful。

grammar: n. 锁；v. 锁上。
collocations: lock the door; a door lock; lock sth with a key
commonMistake: lock 作动词时直接接门或物品作宾语；表示“把某人锁在外面”用 lock sb out。

example.english: Remember to lock the door before you leave.
example.chinese: 离开前记得锁门。

application.prompt: Please ___ the gate after the dog goes inside. A. lock B. open
application.solution: A。解析：狗进去后要把门锁上，用 lock。

grammar: phr. 锁好（建筑物的）门；把……锁起来。
collocations: lock up the shop; lock the house up; lock up a bicycle
commonMistake: lock up 可分开使用：lock the shop up；代词宾语放中间：lock it up。

example.english: The shop owner locks up at nine every evening.
example.chinese: 店主每晚九点锁店。

application.prompt: Before leaving the office, Mina checked every door and ___ the building. A. locked up B. looked up
application.solution: A。解析：检查门后把建筑锁好，用 lock up。

grammar: v. 开锁；解锁；揭开。
collocations: unlock a door; unlock a phone; unlock a secret
commonMistake: unlock 是 lock 的反义动词，表示“开锁”；不要把 un- 后的词误当形容词。

example.english: He used a code to unlock his phone.
example.chinese: 他用密码解锁了手机。

application.prompt: I cannot get into the room until you ___ the door. A. lock B. unlock
application.solution: B。解析：要进入房间，需要把门 unlock（开锁）。

examTags: 词汇·形容词与过去分词
语法·hide 的不规则变化
grammar: adj. 隐藏的；秘密的；也是 hide 的过去分词。hide—hid—hidden。
collocations: a hidden door; hidden treasure; keep sth hidden
commonMistake: hide 的过去分词是 hidden；描述被藏起来的东西可用 hidden，不能写 hided。

example.english: They found a hidden room behind the bookshelf.
example.chinese: 他们在书架后面发现了一间隐藏的房间。

application.prompt: The key was ___ under a flowerpot. A. hid B. hidden
application.solution: B。解析：was 后的被动结构要用过去分词 hidden。

grammar: pron. 没有人；谁也不。作主语时谓语通常用单数。
collocations: nobody knows; nobody was there; nobody else
commonMistake: nobody 表示否定意义，谓语用单数；句中不再与 not 连用。

example.english: Nobody knew where the old map came from.
example.chinese: 没有人知道这张旧地图是从哪里来的。

application.prompt: ___ was at home when I called. A. Nobody B. Nobody were
application.solution: A。解析：nobody 作主语，谓语用单数 was。

grammar: adv. 因此；所以。用于说明结果。
collocations: therefore, we decided; and therefore; it was raining; therefore, ...
commonMistake: therefore 是连接副词；连接两个独立分句时通常用句号或分号，不能只用逗号连接。

example.english: The road was closed; therefore, we took a different route.
example.chinese: 道路封闭了，因此我们走了另一条路线。

application.prompt: The train was delayed; ___, we arrived late. A. however B. therefore
application.solution: B。解析：前句说明火车晚点，后句是其结果，因此用 therefore。

grammar: n. 状态；州；国家；v. 陈述；说明。
collocations: a state of mind; state a reason; the United States
commonMistake: state 作动词表示正式说明；state of mind 表示“精神状态”。

example.english: Please state your name and class on the form.
example.chinese: 请在表格上写明你的姓名和班级。

application.prompt: The report clearly ___ why the plan failed. A. states B. stays
application.solution: A。解析：说明失败原因用 state；主语 report 为单数，故用 states。

grammar: adj. 虚弱的；（能力等）弱的。名词 weakness。
collocations: feel weak; weak eyesight; weak in maths
commonMistake: weak 是形容词；描述某方面薄弱可用 be weak in sth，不要误用 weak at 作固定搭配。

example.english: I felt weak after being ill for several days.
example.chinese: 生病几天后我感到很虚弱。

application.prompt: After the long walk, the tired dog looked ___. A. weak B. weakness
application.solution: A。解析：look 后作表语需要形容词 weak。

grammar: prep./conj./adv. 自……以来；既然；由于。表示起点时常与现在完成时连用。
collocations: since Monday; since I was young; have known sb since 2020
commonMistake: 表示一段时间用 for，表示起点用 since；since 引导原因状语从句时意为“既然”。

example.english: She has lived here since she was five.
example.chinese: 她从五岁起就住在这里。

application.prompt: We have been friends ___ primary school. A. for B. since
application.solution: B。解析：primary school 是时间起点，搭配 since。

grammar: adv. 秘密地；暗中地。
collocations: secretly take a photo; work secretly; secretly hope
commonMistake: secretly 修饰动词；secret 是形容词或名词，不能直接作副词。

example.english: The children secretly prepared a card for their teacher.
example.chinese: 孩子们偷偷为老师准备了一张卡片。

application.prompt: They ___ left a gift on the teacher’s desk. A. secret B. secretly
application.solution: B。解析：修饰动词 left 需用副词 secretly。

examTags: 语法·prove 的词形与结构
grammar: v. 证明；证实；结果是。过去式、过去分词常用 proved，过去分词也可用 proven。
collocations: prove a fact; prove that...; prove to be useful
commonMistake: prove sth to sb 表示“向某人证明某事”；prove 后接宾语时不加介词 to。

example.english: The experiment proved that the water was clean.
example.chinese: 实验证明水是干净的。

application.prompt: The test results ___ that the medicine was safe. A. proved B. proof
application.solution: A。解析：句子需要谓语动词过去式 proved；proof 是名词。

grammar: phr. 站起身来。feet 是 foot 的复数形式。
collocations: get to one’s feet; rise to one’s feet; help sb to their feet
commonMistake: 固定表达用 feet（foot 的复数）；one’s 要随主语改为 my/your/his/her/their。

example.english: The old man slowly got to his feet and waved goodbye.
example.chinese: 老人慢慢站起身来，挥手告别。

application.prompt: After the speech, everyone ___ and clapped. A. got to their foot B. got to their feet
application.solution: B。解析：固定短语为 get to one’s feet；foot 的复数是 feet。

sources.label: Cambridge Dictionary: get to one’s feet

grammar: phr. 一天天；逐日；日渐。可表示变化逐渐发生。
collocations: improve day by day; grow stronger day by day; day by day changes
commonMistake: day by day 表示逐渐变化；every day 仅表示“每天”，不一定强调变化。

example.english: Her English improved day by day.
example.chinese: 她的英语一天天进步。

application.prompt: The patient grew stronger ___ after the operation. A. day by day B. one day
application.solution: A。解析：强调每天逐渐好转，用 day by day。

grammar: n. 准备期；逐步发展；铺垫。
collocations: a build-up to the climax; a gradual build-up; story build-up
commonMistake: build-up 作名词通常带连字符；build up 作动词短语时不带连字符。

example.english: The slow build-up made the ending more exciting.
example.chinese: 缓慢的铺垫让结尾更令人兴奋。

application.prompt: The events before the exciting ending form the story’s ___. A. build-up B. building up
application.solution: A。解析：名词 build-up 表示高潮前逐步形成的铺垫。

grammar: n. （故事、事件等的）高潮；顶点。
collocations: the climax of a story; reach a climax; build up to the climax
commonMistake: climax 表示情节高潮；不要与 climate（气候）混淆。

example.english: The rescue scene is the climax of the novel.
example.chinese: 营救场面是这部小说的高潮。

application.prompt: The most exciting part of the play is its ___. A. climate B. climax
application.solution: B。解析：戏剧中最激动人心的部分是 climax（高潮）。

grammar: n. 影响；结果；效果。
collocations: have an effect on; side effect; cause and effect
commonMistake: effect 通常作名词；affect 常作动词，注意拼写和词性。

example.english: The new rule had a positive effect on the whole team.
example.chinese: 新规定对整个团队产生了积极影响。

application.prompt: Regular reading can have a good ___ on your vocabulary. A. effect B. affect
application.solution: A。解析：形容词 good 后需要名词 effect；affect 通常作动词。

examTags: 语法·in time 与 on time
grammar: phr. 及时；来得及。
collocations: arrive in time; save sb in time; just in time
commonMistake: in time 表示“及时、赶得上”；on time 表示“准时、按计划时间”。

example.english: The doctor arrived in time to help the injured man.
example.chinese: 医生及时赶到，帮助了那名伤者。

application.prompt: The train left early, but we reached the station just ___ to catch it. A. on time B. in time
application.solution: B。解析：火车提前开出时仍赶上了，表示“来得及”用 in time。

grammar: n. 读者；简易读物。
collocations: a regular reader; young readers; a reader of the newspaper
commonMistake: reader 指“读者”或分级读物；read 是动词，reading 可作阅读活动。

example.english: The author answered questions from her young readers.
example.chinese: 作者回答了年轻读者们的问题。

application.prompt: The book is written for young English ___. A. readers B. reading
application.solution: A。解析：介词 for 后表示“英语读者”，用名词 readers。

grammar: n. 图书管理员；图书馆馆长。
collocations: ask the librarian; school librarian; work as a librarian
commonMistake: librarian 是人，library 是地点；不要混淆两者的词尾。

example.english: The librarian helped me find a book about space.
example.chinese: 图书管理员帮我找了一本关于太空的书。

application.prompt: The person who helps visitors find books is the ___. A. library B. librarian
application.solution: B。解析：帮助读者找书的人是 librarian；library 是图书馆。

grammar: v. 认为；仔细考虑。
collocations: consider doing sth; consider sb/sth (to be); consider a question
commonMistake: consider 后接动名词作宾语，不接不定式；表示“认为……”可用 consider sb/sth (to be)...。

example.english: We are considering visiting the city museum this weekend.
example.chinese: 我们正在考虑这周末去参观市立博物馆。

application.prompt: We are ___ joining the book club next term. A. considering B. deciding to
application.solution: A。解析：consider 后接动名词 joining。

grammar: n. 敌人；敌军。复数 enemies。
collocations: an enemy of the country; make an enemy; fight an enemy
commonMistake: enemy 的复数为 enemies（辅音字母加 y 结尾变 ies）。

example.english: The hero refused to treat his enemy cruelly.
example.chinese: 主人公拒绝残忍地对待他的敌人。

application.prompt: The two countries were once ___. A. enemys B. enemies
application.solution: B。解析：enemy 的正确复数形式是 enemies。

grammar: adj. 淘气的；顽皮的。
collocations: a naughty child; be naughty; a naughty joke
commonMistake: naughty 常形容孩子或行为淘气；表示“不听话”也可用 badly behaved。

example.english: The naughty puppy chewed one of my shoes.
example.chinese: 那只淘气的小狗咬坏了我的一只鞋。

application.prompt: The ___ boy hid his sister’s book as a joke. A. naughty B. nervous
application.solution: A。解析：故意藏起妹妹的书来开玩笑，体现淘气，用 naughty。

grammar: adj. 温柔的；温和的；轻柔的。副词 gently。
collocations: a gentle voice; be gentle with; a gentle breeze
commonMistake: gentle 是形容词，修饰动词需用 gently；gentle with sb/sth 表示对……温柔。

example.english: Please be gentle with the young kitten.
example.chinese: 请温柔地对待这只小猫。

application.prompt: The nurse spoke in a ___ voice to calm the child. A. gently B. gentle
application.solution: B。解析：名词 voice 前用形容词 gentle 作定语。

grammar: n. 失败；v. 击败；战胜。
collocations: defeat an opponent; suffer a defeat; defeat the team
commonMistake: defeat 作动词直接接对手；beat 也可表示击败，defeat 不能作“打节拍”。

example.english: Our school team defeated the visitors by two goals.
example.chinese: 我们校队以两球优势击败了客队。

application.prompt: The home team ___ its strongest rivals in the final. A. defeated B. lost
application.solution: A。解析：主队战胜对手，用 defeat；过去式拼写不变加 ed。

grammar: adj. 基本的；初步的。
collocations: basic skills; basic information; the basic idea
commonMistake: basic 是形容词；名词“基础”常用 basis，副词“基本上”用 basically。

example.english: All students need basic computer skills.
example.chinese: 所有学生都需要基本的计算机技能。

application.prompt: The course teaches ___ first-aid skills. A. basically B. basic
application.solution: B。解析：名词 skills 前需要形容词 basic。

grammar: n. 推荐；建议。复数 recommendations。
collocations: a book recommendation; make a recommendation; follow sb’s recommendation
commonMistake: recommendation 是名词；动词是 recommend。注意拼写中有双 m。

example.english: My friend gave me a useful recommendation for a new novel.
example.chinese: 朋友给我推荐了一本值得读的新小说。

application.prompt: The teacher made a ___ about which book to read. A. recommendation B. recommend
application.solution: A。解析：冠词 a 后需名词 recommendation。

grammar: adj. 美国的；美洲的；n. 美国人；美洲人。
collocations: American English; an American writer; American culture
commonMistake: American 可指美国的或美洲的；英语通常说 American English，不要把 American 当语言名。

example.english: The novel was written by an American author.
example.chinese: 这部小说由一位美国作家创作。

application.prompt: Mark Twain was a famous ___ writer. A. America B. American
application.solution: B。解析：修饰 writer 要用形容词 American。

grammar: n. 骨头；骨骼。复数 bones。
collocations: break a bone; bone structure; a fish bone
commonMistake: bone 是可数名词；表示一根骨头需用 a bone。

example.english: The doctor said that no bone was broken.
example.chinese: 医生说没有骨头骨折。

application.prompt: The X-ray showed a small ___ in his arm was broken. A. bone B. blood
application.solution: A。解析：X 光显示手臂的一块骨头骨折，应用 bone。

grammar: n. 怀疑；疑惑；v. 怀疑；不确定。
collocations: without doubt; have no doubt that; doubt whether
commonMistake: 名词短语 without doubt 表示“毫无疑问”；动词 doubt 后可接 whether 引导的从句。

example.english: I have no doubt that she will do well in the exam.
example.chinese: 我确信她会在考试中取得好成绩。

application.prompt: I am not sure the old bridge is safe after the storm, so I ___ it is safe to cross. A. doubt B. decide
application.solution: A。解析：不确定桥是否安全时可说 doubt it is safe；decide 表示作出决定。

grammar: v. 激励；鼓舞；赋予灵感。
collocations: inspire sb to do sth; inspire hope; be inspired by
commonMistake: inspire sb to do sth 表示“鼓舞某人做某事”；不要误写为 inspire sb do sth。

example.english: Her grandmother inspired her to become a doctor.
example.chinese: 她的祖母激励她成为一名医生。

application.prompt: The coach’s words ___ us to keep trying. A. inspiration B. inspired
application.solution: B。解析：句子需要谓语动词；inspire 的过去式为 inspired。

grammar: v. 破坏；摧毁。
collocations: destroy a building; destroy evidence; be destroyed by fire
commonMistake: destroy 是及物动词，后面直接接被破坏的对象，不需加 to。

example.english: The fire destroyed several houses near the river.
example.chinese: 大火烧毁了河边的几栋房屋。

application.prompt: The storm may ___ the old wooden bridge. A. destroy B. damage to
application.solution: A。解析：destroy 后直接接宾语 bridge；damage 也可及物，但 damage to 不符合此处句式。

grammar: n. 介绍；序言；引言。
collocations: an introduction to a book; make an introduction; write an introduction
commonMistake: introduction 是名词，动词为 introduce；谈一本书的引言用 an introduction。

example.english: The introduction explains why the author wrote the book.
example.chinese: 序言解释了作者写这本书的原因。

application.prompt: The first chapter gives readers an ___ to the main characters. A. introduce B. introduction
application.solution: B。解析：冠词 an 后需要名词 introduction。
